decision.reason: Previous run failed only due to unsupported preprocessing fields, so start with a valid text baseline. Headline pairs are best compared via character n-gram TF-IDF difference on the two columns to capture wording variation; logistic regression is a solid first baseline for text classification.

Baseline char-difference TF-IDF scored 0.638, modestly above majority (0.512). The task appears to require detecting subtle semantic/wording contrasts between paired headlines, which char n-grams on the difference capture only weakly. Trying word-level n-grams on the difference signal (capturing shared-meaning vs. changed-word edits) as a complementary baseline; logistic regression with slightly stronger regularization.

Word-level difference TF-IDF reached 0.679 vs 0.638 for char n-grams, indicating word features on the pair difference are informative. The difference-only view discards shared context that may matter for detecting subtle semantic contradictions. Combining both columns (concat) as word n-grams gives the model full-pair signal while n-grams still capture the edit patterns; using class_weight balanced is unnecessary since labels are near-even, so keep logistic regression with moderate regularization.

Best result so far is word n-grams on the difference (0.679); concat was worse (0.659), confirming difference signal is key. Adding character n-grams alongside word n-grams on the difference could capture morphological/subword cues missed by word-only features. Keep logistic regression and increase C slightly to exploit richer feature space.

Word-level difference TF-IDF with logistic regression remains the clear best (0.679); char n-grams (0.638/0.645) and concat (0.659) both trail, confirming the pair-difference word signal is the key feature. With only one step left, refine this winning configuration: a nonlinear random forest on the same word-difference features can capture interactions among edit tokens and word n-grams that a linear model misses, often improving over LR on this kind of contrast classification task.
